newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Gulf Air cuts debt to $923 mln.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Air cuts debt to $923 mln.

text.p: Regional carrier Gulf Air said on Wednesday it had sharply cut its debts to $923 million by the end of June from $1.566 billion in December 1995.

"Gulf Air's indebtedness totalled $1,566 million in December 1995. The management has been able to reduce these debts to $923 million by the end of June 1997," president and chief executive Sheikh Ahmed bin Saif al-Nahayan said in a statement.
"A further reduction is anticipated before the end of 1997, which confirms that Gulf Air is forging ahead on the right track and right direction...," he added.
The airline did not announce its 1996 results. It made a net loss of $159 million in 1995, the worst since the 1990-91 Gulf crisis when it suffered a $100 million deficit.
Manama-based Gulf Air, owned by the governments of Bahrain, Oman, Qatar and Abu Dhabi emirate in the United Arab Emirates, has cut jobs and closed unprofitable routes in efforts to cut losses.
"Gulf Air's capital dropped to approximately 50 million dinars by the end of December 1995," Sheikh Ahmed said.
"But the management has been able to cover losses and increase asset value, raising the capital to 110 million dinars by the end of June 1997," he said without elaborating.
